description:
The transfer arc on the /fly screen for library missions has endpoints pinned to the correct Earth-at-departure and destination-at-arrival positions, but the middle of the arc is always a pure Hohmann-baseline Keplerian ellipse regardless of the mission's actual arrival V-infinity. Missions with high arrival V-infinity (e.g. Mariner 4, ~5.52 km/s) should have a visibly more energetic/bent arc shape, but the arc is identical to a zero-V∞ (Hohmann) baseline.

Expected: When a mission provides flight.arrival.v_infinity_km_s, the /fly transfer arc must be shaped by that value — high V∞ arcs should bend more (the arc deviates from the Hohmann baseline by an amount proportional to the V∞/Hohmann-V∞ ratio). Missions without V∞ data should fall back to the Hohmann baseline ellipse. The arc endpoints must remain pinned to the correct live planet positions at departure and arrival dates.

Acceptance criteria:
- The transfer arc (outbound leg) on /fly must differ from the plain Hohmann baseline when the loaded mission has flight.arrival.v_infinity_km_s > 0, and the deviation must scale with the V∞ ratio [reporter: reporter's follow-up answer: 'The mid-arc bend is wrong because the arrival V-infinity is not being applied. A high arrival V-infinity should bend the middle of the arc away from the baseline (pure-ellipse) shape']
- Missions with no flight.arrival.v_infinity_km_s (or null/undefined) must produce the baseline Hohmann ellipse, unchanged from current behavior [reporter: reporter's follow-up answer: 'a low/zero arrival V-infinity should leave the arc close to the baseline ellipse']
- The arc endpoints must remain at the correct Earth-at-dep_day and destination-at-arrival positions (those endpoints are already correct) [reporter: initial report: 'the endpoints are in the right places']
